ai.title: Ad creative sanitizer expands escape and ignorable stripping
ai.summary: sanitizeAdText in common/src/util/ad-creative-safety.ts now strips C1 control characters and a comprehensive Unicode Default_Ignorable_Code_Point set. Replaces narrow BIDI_OVERRIDE and INVISIBLE regexes with a single explicit DEFAULT_IGNORABLE pattern covering Unicode 16 properties, including variation selectors and tag characters. CSI and OSC regexes updated to match 8-bit escape sequences (, ) alongside standard ESC-prefixed forms. Deterministic across Bun and browser runtimes without relying on runtime Unicode tables.

eli5.text: Ads served through the platform now have stricter cleaning applied to the text they show, so characters that are invisible or could trick a reviewer into approving something that actually looks different are removed before the ad goes live. If you review or approve ad copy, the version you see is now closer to what viewers will actually see, because the cleaning also catches more types of hidden or control characters that used to slip through. The change is part of the core ad-safety handling and applies to ad creative text processing on the shared/common code path. It is live now.

ai.title: Onboarding validation accepts partial submissions and only rejects
ai.summary: `validateOnboardingSubmission` in `common/src/constants/freebuff-onboarding.ts` no longer treats an unanswered question as an error, so a submission with some questions left blank passes validation and only the answered questions are persisted. The function now skips blank answers with if (optionIds.length === 0) continue and returns a submission-level error only when `cleaned.length === 0`, refusing an entirely empty submission with { questionId: null, message: 'Choose at least one answer.' }. This aligns the validator with the append-only option-id design documented in the same file, where skipping a question is a deliberate user choice rather than a client defect.

eli5.text: The free assistant service no longer keeps separate daily usage limits for each model. Previously, some of the smarter AI models (like V4 Pro and GPT-5.6 Luna) had their own strict caps, like only one or two uses per day, separate from your normal usage. Now, those models draw from the same shared daily pool that other models already used, so you can use them more flexibly as long as you have daily sessions left. The documentation across the main guide and the Chinese version was updated to reflect this change, which appears to be live now.

facts: FULL ACCESS ONLY. The limited tier is a separate catalog (LIMITED_FREEBUFF_MODEL_IDS) and is deliberately untouched: those users still get MiMo 2.5 alone, and Flash's pause there is what keeps those sessions free.
This is the FULL-ACCESS pool only. The limited tier meters by region rather than model and reads LIMITED_FREEBUFF_MODEL_IDS, so nothing here reaches it.

The hero is premium, so ALWAYS pass `premiumExhausted` from the live quota snapshot: it flips to FALLBACK_FREEBUFF_MODEL_ID once the daily pool runs out, because the recommended pick has to stay joinable. A caller that omits it will offer a hero whose next send fails admission.

ai.title: Add tracked link placement grain and first-party cohort logging fields
ai.summary: Adds `TRACKED_LINK_PLACEMENT_ID` and `placementSlotLabel` to handle reporting grains outside the buyable `PLACEMENT_SLOTS` catalog, preventing `undefined` labels for external clicks. Normalizes primary allocation percentages to 10,000-bucket basis points via `firstPartyPrimaryBasisPoints` to ensure routing and campaign selection use identical precision. Extends Axiom logging with `first_party_primary_cohort`, `first_party_served_cohort`, and `primary_allocation_invalid` fields to distinguish deliberate control groups from missing data. Updates `common/src/constants/freebuff-placements.ts`, `common/src/util/ad-experiment.ts`, and `common/src/util/axiom-only-log.ts`.

eli5.text: You might have noticed that clicks on special tracked links could previously show up in reports with a blank or missing label. The system now assigns those clicks a consistent, readable name so they are no longer logged as undefined. Separately, the percentage that decides which users see first-party ads is now converted to a shared, high-precision scale used by both ad delivery and campaign selection, preventing small rounding differences from sending a user to two different ad sources. The logging system now separately records the exact cohort a user was chosen for, the cohort that actually served the ad, and whether that allocation was deliberately invalid, so control groups can be distinguished from missing data. This is live today across all surfaces that label placements.
